tickets.text: Generic evaluator overhead in views: the woods' picture view, ~500 ms per figure move after #1. DONE 2026-10-13: a value known to have a type is not walked again for it (#2635 237e5aae74, #2597 e6d1cc500f, comment a8fe28953d / 30f6835b49; dev #2681): Firefox view 563.5 -> 497.5 ms. PROFILED AGAIN 2026-10-13 (node, through evaluate_open as the app runs it; harness ~/.cache/hazel-diag/Test_PicView.timing.re): the view allocates ~1,064 MiB per run, and GC is about as large as its own work. What's left is spread over the evaluator's machinery: the trampoline (Bind/Next nodes, continuations; ~240 MiB), EvaluatorState.update copying the state record every step (~66 MiB), Transition.transition (~129 MiB), string building that is the view's own work (coords, ~76 MiB), fresh ids. Ascription pushing fell 143 -> 61 ms. TRIED, not kept yet: bind(Done(x), f) = f(x): view 407 -> 375 ms in node, ranges overlapping; a stack-depth risk to check (patch ~/.cache/hazel-diag/trampoline_fast_bind.patch). FOUND, load-time only: the first consistent_by_hash miss on the Html types costs tens of ms (memoized for the session after). PER-STEP TUNING 2026-10-13 (his option 1), LOCAL, not pushed: bind(Done(x), f) = f(x) (d0c56fb090, with 2 deep-recursion tests) and a step with no effects only counts (c4e64060f1, EvaluatorState.tick), on perf/2635-per-step (8342); #2597 copies a4b856c543 + 684a75cb2f on perf/2597-per-step. Woods allocation -8% (program 4,334 -> 3,980 MiB, view 1,064 -> 980); Firefox view eval 579 -> 558 ms (-3.6%, 20 moves per build, overlapping). Tests 987 on #2635, 974 on #2597. What is left per step is structural (trampoline nodes, continuations, fresh ids): a design question.
#2597 CI red since 2026-10-11 afternoon: full tests time out at 100 min, quick tests run out of heap. Locally, the whole suite in one process runs out of memory after about 96 min.
The Witch slide's extra 2–3 s over Full Body for the same change: not profiled yet.
The commit path: find which of the request's values are new (about 15 ms of hashing, profiled), and make the commit's redraw cheaper.

Option C from issue 005: remember HazelDOM's virtual DOM per Html subterm, so an unchanged part of a view is not converted again and virtual_dom's diff skips it. PARKED 2026-10-12: measured, it would save at most about 2% of the main thread in the woods. A profiled figure move (2 runs, 4.4 and 4.1 s): Html to virtual DOM 1.1%, diff and patch 0.9%, browser layout and paint 1.4%, GC 21%, evaluating the view about 50% (about 69% with its GC), the app's own update machinery about 25%. On Kids' Choice it was 8 of 104 ms (issue 001). It would also need a content hash as its key, since the woods' shapes are fresh objects each time, and handlers that find the current state at event time. The lever is evaluating the view: #1, #2, #18.
Measure the size of view samples on the wire (not trimmed as the result is) and the memory of the shared-value tables and per-object hashes.
Statics counts on dev: the analyses-per-expression counter and Test_StaticsPasses from #2635 (bd90642654, da3251d3e5), with a small corpus subset in the quick suite.
A budget on a slide: the evaluator's work after a figure move in the woods, where reuse failed before #2675.
Byte budgets: elaboration sizes on dev, and the worker's message sizes for a fixed interaction.
Ask the maintainers to require the test jobs for merging into dev: today no check is required, so a red budget is a signal, not a gate.
A timing report that informs and doesn't fail: base and head on one runner, repeated, phase by phase, perhaps from #2161's harness (David's call).

Option B from issue 005: evaluate each livelit's view in the worker, keep the last Html sent per livelit, and post patches to it, so view evaluation leaves the main thread. Needs the view runner (ViewCmdRunner) in the worker, a patch format, an element on the page that owns each livelit's DOM and applies patches, and handlers dispatched by id. Keep the page's own path for an interaction's immediate redraw, or every drag waits a round trip. Its condition is now met (2026-10-12, see #10): evaluating the view is about 69% of the main thread in a woods figure move, and C would save about 2%. Weigh it against making the view itself cheaper first (#1, #2).

Budgets harder to fool (issue 006's update, a count is not a time): count the call memo's own work (the nodes its keys put in form) and, if js_of_ocaml can report it, memory allocated, beside the evaluator's steps.

UX mode re-elaborates an open cell's item with fresh ids on every change (the drawn cell in issue 008's B), so its parts never match by hash and fall to the reuse check's slow path. Keep the ids stable when a cell is analyzed again.

The autosave in UX mode (save_current / persist_divided: the divided program printed to text and stored, 0.55 s profiled) landed inside a slider change in issue 008's B. With #6's fix the change ends first, so it no longer does, but it is still 0.55 s on the main thread about a second after every edit, where the next drag can meet it. Save when idle, or save only the changed cell.

Open cells draw their livelit views without the view memo (live_html, 449 ms per change profiled in issue 008's B with #6's fix), where the whole-program editor uses memo_view (163 ms in C). Give cells the memo. (Corrected 2026-10-12: B's 0.48 s of of_segment was the autosave printing text, not the cells' code views.)

Code-driven tests of the outline modes: a URL parameter (or test hook) that opens a slide in UX mode with chosen GUI rows, so a script reaches issue 008's B without clicking through the outline. Matthew: "let's consider that too with our UX feature".

The page's incremental stream collector (StreamCollector.Inc.fresh) indexes the whole elaboration again for every new evaluation, once per slider change: 204 ms profiled per change in C (Full Body, dev mode). DONE ON #2635 2026-10-13: 8717564a5f stops the walk at patterns and types: 115 ms profiled, clock not detectable (issue 008). REMAINING: map_term still rebuilds every expression node, plus Id.Map inserts. Further: a hashtable, or the worker tags each entry with its enclosing entry so the page needs no index.

closed_tickets.text: The ^picture view in the woods: parts 1–3 DONE 2026-10-12, a woods figure move's redraw from a median of 2.20 s to 1.41 s. Part 1: a Drawing.frame sets the view box (#2597 86e3ea9a9f, b5edde9da3; #2635 6f1d7fdc5e, 44d8ab2225). Part 2: a cheaper coords (#2597 44928f5fdd; #2635 ba72773d46), view steps −26% but time −6%. Part 3: an ascription pushed through a value gives the value back when it already has the type, instead of copying it (#2597 1fa1384445; #2635 57c928cef4). The picture's view on a move to a new size went from about 725–830 ms to 520–650; revisits stay about 210 ms; Kids' Choice is unchanged. That gave the memo cheap keys and kept its hits. Measured and not kept: a key budget (it lost the revisits) and a cache of pushes (nothing over copy-on-change). What is left of the view is the evaluator's own work, about 500 ms: see #2. Close #1?
closed_tickets.outcome: Three fixes, on #2597 and #2635: a Drawing.frame sets the view box, a cheaper coords, and an ascription pushed through a value gives the value back when it already has the type. A woods figure move's redraw went from a median of 2.20 s to 1.41 s. Written up in #2609 finding 29 and issue 004's update. What was left of the view became #2.

closed_tickets.text: #2597's IncrEval.reuse_check never compares lexemes: it lacks 7de3875cd8 ("Invalidate incremental-eval reuse on lexeme-only edits", in dev and #2635), so editing @@ to @@@ in place can show the stale operator's result. Port it in the one-walk form from perf/2635-reuse-one-walk (#6), so #2597 doesn't pick up the quadratic cost with it.
closed_tickets.outcome: Its premise was wrong: #2597 has no lexemes (it lacks 500c466b44) and makes an unknown operator a hole of its operands, so @@ and @@@ give the same term. Issue 008 got dated corrections.
